page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-16 is a network-optimized virtual server instance equipped with 16 dedicated virtual CPU cores operating on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 60 GB of system memory, providing an even 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This dedicated processor provisioning ensures that computing cores are not subject to CPU credit exhaustion or neighbor contention, delivering predictable compute execution across all allocated threads.

The instance profile omits physical accelerators and direct-attached storage. There are no GPUs provisioned on this configuration, focusing computational throughput strictly on traditional x86_64 instructions. Local solid-state storage is absent, meaning workloads must utilize remote block storage or cloud storage buckets for filesystem persistence. Network configuration does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external IP reservations or private network routing for internet-facing connectivity.

From a resource and infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the balanced ratio of approximately four gigabytes of memory per core makes the configuration cost-efficient for standard enterprise tasks without paying for excessive unused memory headroom. The platform is well suited for network traffic routing, distributed backend APIs, container orchestration worker nodes, middleware integration tiers, and general-purpose web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-16 is a virtual machine within the network-optimized server family, engineered for distributed workloads that prioritize network communication and reliable processing. The configuration incorporates 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture and 60 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This instance type contains zero onboard graphics accelerators and includes no local storage volumes, relying entirely on networked storage subsystems for persistent disk operations. From a resource perspective, the instance provides a balanced compute-to-memory profile without overcommitting hardware resources. The dedicated allocation guarantees consistent execution environments free from shared-core contention. Given its balanced ratio of processing capacity to memory, the instance is structured to support enterprise network appliances, distributed web services, backend application servers, and general-purpose containerized tasks requiring stable multi-core processing throughput.
